blocks.title: Software as a Service (SaaS)
blocks.text: SaaS provides software applications hosted and managed by the provider; users subscribe and use them over the internet, with no hardware to manage and no software updates to install.

Google Workspace (formerly G Suite) includes Gmail, Google Docs and Google Drive; Microsoft Office 365 and Salesforce are other examples. The book notes that Salesforce is a leading SaaS provider of customer relationship management (CRM) used by over 150,000 companies, and that cloud services are priced by usage, pay as you go (Did You Know).

blocks.prompt: Which is NOT a type of cloud service named in the chapter: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS or BaaS (MCQ 5)?
blocks.explanation: (d) Blockchain as a Service (BaaS) is not one of the three main types taught, although some providers do offer it.

blocks.prompt: Class activity: research a cloud provider such as AWS, Azure or Google Cloud and describe a real-world use.
blocks.explanation: For example, a company can host its website on AWS virtual servers (IaaS), keep backups in cloud storage, and let staff use Gmail and Google Docs (SaaS); students should present the provider, the service type and what it saves.

items: SaaS: ready-made software over the internet (Gmail, Office 365, Salesforce).
